ss-220559716.blurb: Relationships don't decay. We learn what they were.
ss-220559716.rationale: The most rigorous piece in the corpus: concrete mechanistic models, quantified results, and five falsifiable predictions. Counterintuitive findings (selection not growth; 7x reconciliation asymmetry) are clearly argued.

ss-208463566.blurb: Test a model's values, not its outputs.
ss-208463566.rationale: Clear, original framing of the scalable-oversight problem with a concrete proposal (structurally novel moral dilemmas probing incentive, not behavior). Strongest pure AI-safety piece; would benefit from a worked example.

ss-220251918.blurb: AI broke the resume. Trust is what's left.
ss-220251918.rationale: Tight, well-structured argument with a memorable thesis and a practical takeaway. Also posted to LessWrong.

ss-209224664.rationale: Good taxonomy (shared core objectives vs learned heuristics) that connects human moral error to alignment. Some failure modes overlap.

ss-208418808.blurb: A letter to Marcus about the minds we're building.
ss-208418808.rationale: Moving and well-written; bridges philosophy and alignment. Argument is more rhetorical than rigorous ('control is impossible' is asserted, not shown).

ss-210543088.blurb: Check the goal before the data.
ss-210543088.rationale: Clean incentive -> objective -> context -> decision pipeline and a useful self-reinforcing-loop insight. Short and focused.

ss-206772437.rationale: Sharp contrarian thesis that builds to a real conclusion about autonomy. A few leaps (morality diverges 'Not might. Will.') are asserted.

ss-215583264.blurb: What a job really buys from you.
ss-215583264.rationale: Useful, practical framework for evaluating labs, but familiar econ (principal-agent, opportunity cost) and list-heavy formatting.

ss-213921144.blurb: Decide later. Sixteen biases, sixteen fixes.
ss-213921144.rationale: Opening section on aimed reasoning is good; the bulk is a catalog of well-known biases with standard fixes, so originality is lower.

ss-218633709.blurb: Value moves to what's hard to fake.
ss-218633709.rationale: Reasonable synthesis with a crisp core rule, but largely consensus forecasting and list-driven.

ss-210377028.rationale: Interesting 'attention as obsession' idea, but the first third repeats Love, Aurelius nearly verbatim and the core idea stays speculative.

ss-207055706.rationale: The strongest creative work: real characters, specific details (the withheld laugh, the thirtieth Tuesday), and a structure that earns its closing aphorisms.

ss-213722983.blurb: Debts, and a parable about worth.
ss-213722983.rationale: Distinctive voice and confident, quotable lines ('If a doctrine does not change what a man does on an ordinary Tuesday then it is jewelry'). Ambitious form, mostly pulled off.

ss-211829148.blurb: Life isn't short. We waste it.
ss-211829148.rationale: Seneca-inflected essay with real rhetorical force and a clear turn toward the 'pull you cannot explain'. Theme is familiar but the execution is strong.

ss-220000849.blurb: A self-portrait in the third person.
ss-220000849.rationale: Honest and self-aware, with its best lines on mistaking beauty for truth. Benefits from knowing the author.

ss-216230747.rationale: Warm and sincere with a lovely central image; drifts into abstraction ('majesty so pure') in the back half.

ss-207827995.blurb: Focus × time × the room you're in.
ss-207827995.rationale: Short and punchy but the idea is well-trodden and the 'formula' is not developed beyond the anecdotes.

ss-221421459.blurb: Sycophancy shows up in the last layers.
ss-221421459.rationale: First hands-on interp experiment in the corpus with a clean neutral/bait design and a clear finding. Thin evidence (20 prompts, one behavioral flip, logit lens only, no error bars or ablation) and the layer-27 circuit claim outruns the data; the piece ends abruptly.
